newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of E. Asia says China's asset rules too tough.
newsitem.headline: Bank of E. Asia says China's asset rules too tough.

text.p: China's asset requirement for foreign banks setting up sub-branches may be too onerous for banks in Hong Kong and Southeast Asia, said David Li, deputy chairman and chief executive at Bank of East Asia.
China has stipulated that foreign banks wishing to set up branches in the country must maintain net assets of at least US$20 billion in the country.

Li said that in a recent trip to China in his capacity as chairman of the Chinese Banking Association, he asked Peoples Bank of China governor Dai Xianglong to consider reducing the minimum asset requirement because he believed "Hong Kong and Southeast Asia registered banks cannot reach this amount."
Li was speaking to reporters at a signing ceremony for the bank's recent floating rate certificate of deposit issue.
Bank of East Asia currently operates six branches and six representative offices in mainland China and has applied to open a branch in the Pudong district of Shanghai.
Li said Bank of East Asia's China operations are expected to contribute 30-40 percent of the the group's profits in three to four years compared with 13 percent at end-1995.
